newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt finds offshore gas reserves.
newsitem.headline: Egypt finds offshore gas reserves.

text.p: U.S. Amoco Corp and a local subsidiary of Italy's Agip SpA have found more gas in the Mediterranean off Port Said, the Egyptian oil ministry said on Monday.

A discovery well named Tuna tested at 16 million cubic feet of gas a day, it said. It is in the Temsah concession operated by Amoco and Agip's subsidiary, International Egyptian Oil Company (IEOC), the ministry added.
"An oil-bearing layer was found at the depth of between 1,130 and 1,275 metres," it said in a statement. "The discovery is a successful result applying 3D seismic surveying."
The well is 40 miles off Port Said at the northern mouth of the Suez Canal and about six miles northeast of the Temsah field.

Amoco has been trying to establish the size of the Temsah field. "It may be part of a much larger contiguous field and there's the possibility of large fields in deeper water in our and in other concessions," said Amoco Egypt vice president Gary Bose in an interview in August.
